title: Oral Expression · L1 Greetings and polite expressions

questions.stem: Which greetings belong to a formal register?
questions.explanation: The lecture contrasts "Hi there!" (informal) with "Good morning, Madam." (formal); the answer key adds "How do you do?" as very formal, used on first meeting.

questions.stem: "How do you do?" is, according to the answer key:
options: A question about the patient's health that needs a detailed answer
questions.explanation: It is listed as very formal, on first meeting. To ask about health, the lecture uses "How are you feeling today?".

questions.stem: Which expressions are closing phrases from the lecture's vocabulary list?
options: Excuse me, could I ask you something?
questions.explanation: Take care / Get well soon / See you tomorrow close an exchange; "Excuse me, could I ask you something?" opens a polite request.

questions.stem: A patient arrives at reception. According to the reading text, the receptionist should:
options: Greet the patient before asking for any paperwork
Ask for the paperwork first, then greet
Use the patient's first name immediately
Use the patient's name with Mr or Mrs once known
questions.explanation: Always greet first. Use Mr/Mrs unless the patient invites you to use their first name.

questions.stem: Why does the text recommend "Mr" or "Mrs" rather than the first name?
options: The first name may be used if the patient invites you to
First names are forbidden in hospitals
questions.explanation: Answer key: because it is more respectful, and Mr/Mrs should be used unless the patient invites you to use their first name.

questions.stem: If a patient looks anxious, the text advises you to:
options: Switch to a very formal register
questions.explanation: Slow down your speech and keep your tone warm.

questions.stem: In the model dialogue, which lines are polite requests?
options: May I have your name, please?
Please take a seat; the doctor will call you shortly.
Good morning. How can I help you?
questions.explanation: "May I…, please?" and "Please take a seat" are requests. "Thank you very much" is thanks; "Good morning" is the greeting.

questions.stem: The guided speaking practice keeps which structure for every new situation?
questions.explanation: The dialogue is adapted (elderly patient arriving late, worried parent, visitor) while keeping the greeting–request–thanks structure.

options: The day and time of the appointment
questions.explanation: The task asks for a greeting, the appointment details, a practical instruction and a polite closing, using at least three polite expressions (60–80 words).

questions.stem: In the listening task (British Council, Hospital Scene 1), what is happening?
options: Ashlie and Stephen are at the hospital
Mostly very formal language is used
The characters are at a pharmacy
questions.explanation: The answer key: the characters are at the hospital, where Stephen is being examined; expect simple, everyday greetings rather than very formal language.

questions.stem: Which reply is appropriate to "Thank you very much"?
questions.explanation: The vocabulary list pairs "Thank you very much." with "You're welcome."
